entry: American video game developer, publisher and digital distribution company, based in Bellevue, Washington. Founded in 1996 by former [[Microsoft]] employees [[Gabe Newell]] and Mike Harrington, Valve released the first-person shooter *[[Half-Life (video game)|Half-Life]]* in 1998, a critical and commercial success. Its franchises include Counter-Strike, Portal and Team Fortress, and it operates the digital distribution service [[Steam (service)|Steam]], launched in 2003. Most of Valve's revenue comes from Steam. Valve uses a flat organizational structure in which employees choose their own projects. [[Lawsuit|Antitrust lawsuits]] allege that Steam's pricing policies stifle competition; Valve counters that consumers benefit from its access and library.

Mythical creature that subsists by feeding on the vital essence, usually blood, of humans. In European folklore, vampires are undead humanoids that visit loved ones and cause mischief or deaths in the neighborhoods they inhabited in life. The term was first popularized in Western Europe after 18th-century reports of mass hysteria in [[Eastern Europe|Southeastern and Eastern Europe]], where suspected vampires were sometimes pierced with stakes. In modern times the vampire is generally held to be fictitious; early folk belief has sometimes been ascribed to ignorance of decomposition after death. The charismatic vampire of modern fiction began with "The Vampyre" (1819) by John Polidori. [[Bram Stoker]]'s novel *[[Dracula]]* (1897) provided the basis of the modern vampire legend, and the figure remains a dominant one in horror.

Subfamily of bats that feed exclusively on blood. Vampire bats (Desmodontinae) are leaf-nosed bats of the family Phyllostomidae, found in Central and South America. Three extant species, the common vampire bat (*Desmodus rotundus*), the hairy-legged vampire bat (*Diphylla ecaudata*) and the white-winged vampire bat (*Diaemus youngi*), are the only mammals that feed solely on blood, a diet called hematophagy. Their short muzzles, cutting front teeth and pit organs that detect warm blood vessels help them locate prey. Salivary anticoagulants such as draculin prevent clotting for up to several hours. Vampire bats are highly social, roosting in colonies of dozens to thousands and sharing food by regurgitation. They serve as vectors for [[Rabies|rabies]] and other pathogens, posing challenges to agriculture and wildlife, while their saliva compounds hold promise for anticoagulant therapies.

Type of [[Vehicle|road vehicle]] used for transporting goods or people. Vans range from microvans, which carry small loads or passengers, to panel vans based on passenger car platforms and used mainly for cargo. Larger vans with passenger seats transport students, and specially equipped vans serve television stations as mobile studios. Postal services and courier companies use large step vans to deliver packages. The word is a contraction of caravan, and the earliest English records of a van as a vehicle date from the mid-19th century, when it meant a covered wagon for goods. Usage varies by country. In Australia, van often means a minivan or passenger minibus, while in British English it refers only to vehicles that carry goods, and minivans are called people-carriers.

Zone of energetic charged particles, mostly from the [[Solar wind|solar wind]], trapped around [[Earth]] by its magnetic field. Earth has two main belts, extending about 640 to 58,000 km above the surface. Named after James Van Allen, who described them in 1958, the belts were confirmed that year by Explorer 1 and Explorer 3. They endanger [[Satellite|satellites]], which need shielding near the zone. Apollo astronauts crossing the belts received a very low, harmless dose. In 2013 the Van Allen Probes detected a transient third belt that persisted for four weeks.

American hard rock band formed in Pasadena, California, in 1972. Credited with restoring [[Rock music|hard rock]] to prominence, it was known for energetic live shows and the guitar virtuosity of Eddie Van Halen. Its 1984 album produced the band's only number-one single on the Billboard Hot 100, "Jump". After David Lee Roth left in 1985, Sammy Hagar fronted four U.S. number-one albums. Van Halen disbanded following Eddie's death in 2020, having sold more than 80 million albums worldwide.

Northern Irish singer and songwriter whose recording career began in the 1960s. He rose to prominence as lead singer of the [[Belfast]] R&B band Them, which recorded "Gloria", and his 1967 single "Brown Eyed Girl" was a solo hit. *Astral Weeks* (1968) was initially a poor seller but is now regarded as a classic, and *Moondance* (1970) established him as a major artist. His work blends soul and [[Rhythm and blues|rhythm and blues]] with lengthy, spiritually inspired pieces influenced by Celtic tradition and [[Jazz|jazz]].

Distance-dependent [[Intermolecular force|intermolecular]] interaction between atoms or molecules, not arising from a chemical bond. Named after Dutch physicist [[Johannes Diderik van der Waals]], the force is comparatively weak and vanishes quickly at longer distances. It arises from transient shifts in electron density that induce charges in nearby particles, and at very short distances it becomes repulsive. The force is usually described as a combination of London dispersion forces, Debye forces and the Keesom force. It underlies many properties of organic compounds and molecular solids, including their solubility.

Chemical element with symbol V and atomic number 23, a hard, silvery-grey, malleable [[Transition metal|transition metal]]. The pure metal is rarely found in nature, and an oxide layer somewhat stabilizes it against further oxidation. Spanish scientist Andrés Manuel del Río first identified its compounds in 1801, but his claim was retracted after the element was mistaken for impure chromium. In 1831 Swedish chemist Nils Gabriel Sefström rediscovered it and named it after the Norse goddess Vanadís, for the many colorful compounds it forms. Henry Enfield Roscoe isolated the pure metal later in the 19th century. Vanadium occurs in about 65 minerals and fossil fuel deposits. Approximately 93% of it is used in steel alloys, such as high-speed tool steels. Vanadium pentoxide is an important catalyst in the production of [[Sulfuric acid|sulfuric acid]], and some ocean organisms use vanadium as an active center of enzymes.

Major seaport city in the Lower Mainland of [[British Columbia]], Canada. The city had 662,248 residents in the 2021 census, making it the most populous in the province. Greater Vancouver had 2.6 million people that year, the third-largest metropolitan area in Canada after [[Toronto]] and [[Montreal]]. Vancouver has the highest population density in Canada and is one of its most ethnically and linguistically diverse cities. It is consistently ranked among the most livable cities, though it is also one of the most expensive. The city's large natural seaport on the [[Pacific Ocean|Pacific Ocean]] anchors its economy, along with [[Forestry|forestry]] and tourism. The modern city was renamed Vancouver in 1886 through a deal with the Canadian Pacific Railway, and it is nicknamed Hollywood North for its film production.

Largest island in [[British Columbia]], Canada, in the northeastern Pacific Ocean. It is 456 km long and covers 31,815.31 km² (12,283.96 sq mi) according to the United States Geological Survey. The island is the most populous along the west coasts of the Americas, with 864,864 people in 2021. Nearly half of them live in Greater Victoria, the provincial capital at the island's southern tip. Its name commemorates 1792 negotiations between Spanish and British commanders, including [[Vancouver|George Vancouver]].

East Germanic tribe, first mentioned by Roman writers in the 1st century. Under King Genseric they crossed from the [[Iberian Peninsula|Iberia]] into North Africa in 429, and by 439 they had formed a kingdom covering the Roman province of Africa and several Mediterranean islands. The Vandals fended off several Roman attempts to recapture Africa and sacked the city of Rome in 455. Their kingdom collapsed in the Vandalic War of 533–534, when forces of Emperor [[Justinian I|Justinian I]] reconquered North Africa for the [[Roman Empire|Eastern Roman Empire]]. [[Renaissance|Renaissance]] writers cast the Vandals as barbarians, giving English the word vandalism, though some modern historians stress their continuation of Roman culture.

American family that gained prominence during the [[Gilded Age]] through the shipping and railroad empire of [[Cornelius Vanderbilt]]. The family was once the wealthiest in the United States, and Cornelius's son William Henry Vanderbilt acquired the fortune after his father's death in 1877. Its members built grand mansions in [[New York City|New York City]], summer cottages in Newport, Rhode Island, and the palatial Biltmore House in Asheville, North Carolina. After the mid-20th century most of the family's houses were sold or turned into museums. Contemporary descendants include the journalist [[Anderson Cooper]].

French singer, model and actress who achieved international fame at 14 with the single "Joe le taxi" (1987), which was number one in France for 11 weeks. At 18 she won the César Award for Most Promising Actress for *Noce blanche*. Her film roles include *Élisa* (1995) with [[Gérard Depardieu]] and *Girl on the Bridge* (1999). Musicians including [[Serge Gainsbourg]] and [[Lenny Kravitz]] have cited her work as an inspiration. She has been a spokesmodel for Chanel since 1991.

British actress and activist whose career spans eight decades. She won an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for *Julia* (1977) and a Tony Award for *Long Day's Journey into Night* (2003). She is the daughter of Sir Michael Redgrave. Her political activism, which she says opposes fascism and racism, has drawn controversy and boycotts of her performances; critics have charged some of her positions with antisemitic undertones.

Spice derived from the cured seed pods of orchids of the genus *Vanilla*, chiefly the flat-leaved *V. planifolia* of Mexico and Central America. The Totonac people were among the first to cultivate it, and the Aztecs flavored chocolate drinks with it. [[Hernán Cortés]] is credited with introducing vanilla to Europe in the 1520s. Because vanilla is not self-pollinating, the plant requires pollination by hand; in 1841 Edmond Albius, an enslaved 12-year-old on the island of [[Réunion]], discovered a method that allowed cultivation beyond Mexico. [[Madagascar]] and Indonesia produce two-thirds of the world's supply. By weight, vanilla is the second-most expensive spice after [[Saffron|saffron]], because its pods are labor-intensive to produce.

Archipelagic country of volcanic islands in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, in the [[Melanesia]] region of [[Oceania]]. It lies about 1,750 km east of northern Australia. The islands were first settled about 3,000 years ago by people of the Lapita culture. The first Europeans to visit were a Spanish expedition led by Fernandes de Queirós in 1606. France and the United Kingdom claimed parts of the archipelago in the 1880s and in 1906 agreed to jointly manage it as the New Hebrides under an Anglo-French condominium. Independence came in 1980 as the Republic of Vanuatu, and the country is a member of the [[United Nations]] and the [[Commonwealth of Nations]].

Substance in the [[Gas|gas]] phase at a [[Temperature|temperature]] below its critical temperature, so that it can be [[Condensation|condensed]] to a [[Liquid|liquid]] by increasing pressure alone. A vapor may coexist with its liquid or solid phase in equilibrium, and the vapor pressure of a liquid or solid is its equilibrium pressure at a specific temperature. Water vapor condenses into [[Fog|fog]] and clouds when its partial pressure is raised enough. Vapor is central to evaporation and [[Distillation|distillation]]. A vapor differs from an [[Aerosol|aerosol]], which is a suspension of tiny particles of liquid or solid in a gas. Mercury-vapor and sodium-vapor lamps produce light from atoms in excited states.

Critically endangered [[Porpoise|porpoise]] endemic to the northern end of the [[Gulf of California]] in [[Mexico]]. It is the smallest living [[Cetacean|cetacean]], with females reaching 150 cm (4.9 ft) in length. The steep decline in its numbers is driven mainly by bycatch in gillnets from the illegal totoaba fishery, since the totoaba's swim bladder is valued in [[Traditional Chinese medicine|traditional Chinese medicine]]. Vaquitas are generally seen alone or in pairs, and females are larger than males. The name is Spanish for "little cow".

Historic city on the left bank of the [[Ganges]] River in northern India, in the state of [[Uttar Pradesh]]. Known in ancient times as Kashi, it is one of the world's oldest continually inhabited cities and a center of Hindu pilgrimage, death and mourning. Its many ghats, or riverside steps, are where pilgrims perform rituals and where Hindus cremate their dead, most notably at the Manikarnika Ghat. Notable temples include the Kashi Vishwanath Temple of [[Shiva]]. Silk weaving, carpets and tourism employ many local people. In 1916 Annie Besant and Madan Mohan Malviya founded Banaras Hindu University, and the Benares gharana style of playing the tabla was developed in the city.

Star whose brightness, as seen from [[Earth]], changes over time. The variation may be intrinsic, when the star's luminosity itself changes as it swells and shrinks, or extrinsic, when an orbiting companion eclipses it. Changes range from under an hour to multiple years. Most stars oscillate to some degree; the [[Sun|Sun]] varies by about 0.1% over its 11-year solar cycle, while a [[Supernova|supernova]] can briefly outshine an entire galaxy. The first documented periodic variable was the eclipsing binary Algol. Cepheid variables were shown in 1912 to have a period–luminosity relationship, which made them useful for measuring distances to galaxies. Of the 58,200 variable stars cataloged as of 2023, the most common are pulsating variables.

Statistical measure of how far a set of numbers spreads from its average. For a random variable X, variance is the [[Expected value|expected value]] of the squared deviation from the mean, and the [[Standard deviation|standard deviation]] is its square root. Variance is written as σ² and is non-negative, with zero meaning that all values are identical. Its units are the square of the data's units, which is why the standard deviation is commonly reported. Its advantage is that it is easier to manipulate algebraically; the variance of a sum of uncorrelated random variables equals the sum of their variances. Population variance uses all observations, while sample variance estimates it from a subset. Variance is central to [[Statistics|statistics]], including descriptive statistics and hypothesis testing.

Fatal [[Prion|prion]] disease of the brain, linked mainly to eating beef tainted with [[Bovine spongiform encephalopathy|bovine spongiform encephalopathy]] (BSE). Initial symptoms include psychiatric problems, behavioral changes and painful sensations. Later stages bring poor coordination, dementia and involuntary movements, and average life expectancy after symptoms begin is 13 months. It was first identified in 1996 by the National CJD Surveillance Unit in Edinburgh, Scotland, and 178 cases had been recorded in the [[United Kingdom|United Kingdom]] as of 2020. The typical age of onset is under 30. Treatment is supportive, and diagnosis relies on clinical features and tests such as brain biopsy.

Indian actor who works primarily in [[Hindi|Hindi]] films, one of India's highest-paid actors. He is the son of film director David Dhawan. He made his acting debut in 2012 with [[Karan Johar]]'s teen drama *Student of the Year*, after working as an assistant director on *My Name Is Khan*. He rose to prominence in romantic comedies such as *Humpty Sharma Ki Dulhania* (2014) and the action comedy *Dilwale* (2015), and he earned praise for *Badlapur* (2015) and *October* (2018). He is also a prominent celebrity endorser for several brands.

Portuguese mariner, explorer and nobleman. In 1497–1499 he led the first voyage to link Europe and Asia by an ocean route around the southern tip of Africa, landing at Kozhikode on 20 May 1498. The route, around the [[Cape of Good Hope|Cape of Good Hope]], let the [[Portuguese Empire|Portuguese]] bypass Arab trade networks and obtain spices such as pepper and cinnamon, which Portugal monopolized for decades. He led two of the Portuguese India Armadas, the first and the fourth, and was appointed Governor of India in 1524 with the title of Viceroy. He was ennobled as Count of Vidigueira in 1519. The national epic *Os Lusíadas* was written in his honor by [[Luís de Camões|Luís de Camões]].
